title: Invited, Lord, by Boundless Grace
description: Invited, Lord, by Boundless Grace in Tonic Solfa to MELCOMBE, doh is Eb: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 4 verses and a piano.
about: Emanuel Cronenwett wrote these words. They were printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (St. Louis, 1927), as hymn 438.
The book printed the words without tunes, marked Long Metre (8.8.8.8), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to MELCOMBE; any other Long Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: In-vit-ed, Lord, by bound-less grace, I stood a guest be-fore Thy face; As host Thou spread’st no com-mon food; Here is Thy bo-dy and Thy blood!

lines: I stood a guest before Thy face;
As host Thou spread’st no common food;
Here is Thy body and Thy blood!
Where pardon, peace, and life are spent!
This bread and cup my lips have pressed;
Thou blessedst, and my soul is blessed.
Now lettest Thou Thy guest depart
With full assurance in his heart;
For such communion, Lord, with Thee
May a new life my offering be!
When Thou shalt in Thy glory come
To gather all Thy people home,
Then let me, as Thy heavenly guest,
In anthems praise Thee with the blest!

licence: Public domain: Emanuel Cronenwett died in 1931.
credits: Words by Emanuel Cronenwett (1841–1931), public domain, as printed in the Evangelical Lutheran Hymn-Book (1927); set to MELCOMBE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
